messages:
jordan-cust: Hi team — getting a 401 invalid_api_key when calling the hosted API after creating a key via our org SSO flow. Happening from our CI job, started ~10m ago.

jordan-cust: curl we run (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sso_sk_ABCDEF...' \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large","input":"hello"}'
```

jordan-cust: response body: `{\"error\":{\"type\":\"invalid_api_key\",\"message\":\"unauthorized\"}}`

jordan-cust: The key was created by our org admin via SSO -> Developer Keys -> Create (name: CI-runner). We didn't opt for "dedicated" or anything.

nina-support: thanks for the repro, jordan-cust. quick q: is your tenant using a region-restricted key or Dedicated project? and can you paste the first 8 chars of the key id (no full secret)?

jordan-cust: key id prefix: sso_sk_ABCD1234

nina-support: got it. two quick checks: 1) confirm you're hitting the hosted endpoint (api.redwood.ai) and not a dedicated/private host; 2) confirm the key isn't a short-lived SSO one that needs an exchange. can you run curl with `-v` and paste request headers (you can redact token)?

jordan-cust: attaching the verbose headers output (redacted):
```
> POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> Authorization: Bearer sso_sk_ABCD1234...
> Content-Type: application/json
> User-Agent: curl/7.68.0
```

nina-support: thanks. that looks fine on surface. tagging @tyler-eng to check logs for that key prefix — possible policy/scope mismatch.

tyler-eng: looking now — searching auth logs for key prefix `sso_sk_ABCD1234`.

deploy-bot: [auth-log] 2026-03-09T12:19:07Z key=sso_sk_ABCD1234 action=auth_check result=deny reason=scope_mismatch details="key scoped for org-admin:impersonation, not api:invoke"

tyler-eng: ok logs show this key was minted as an SSO admin/impersonation key (used for user session exchange) and does NOT carry the `api:invoke` scope required for hosted API calls. so API returns invalid_api_key because policy denies token for that route.

nina-support: short-term options: 1) generate a proper service key from the Admin Console -> Developer Keys -> Service keys (ensure "API calls" scope), or 2) use the SSO exchange flow to mint a short-lived token with api:invoke scope (if you intended that flow).

jordan-cust: we thought the SSO "create key" button made a service key. looks like our admin used the wrong flow. any docs link to the correct flow?

nina-support: yes — see docs: https://docs.redwood.ai/auth/service-keys (high level: Admins -> Developer Keys -> Create -> choose "Service key (API)" not the "SSO session/impersonation" option).

tyler-eng: to repro locally: create an impersonation key in console and call hosted endpoint — you'll get the same deny. sample log line in case you want to grep: `auth:deny reason=scope_mismatch key_prefix=sso_sk_`

nina-support: if you want us to rotate/create a proper key for you we can provision a scoped service key and drop it into your org console, or guide admin to create one. do you want us to create it?

jordan-cust: please create one, that'd be faster. we need CI to be unblocked.

nina-support: filing a quick internal request. tagging eng to generate ephemeral service key for org org-773.

tyler-eng: created service key prefix svc_sk_XYZ98765 with api:invoke + embeddings scopes. I posted it to the org console under Developer Keys -> CI-runner-service (admin only). pls ask admin to copy.

jordan-cust: admin confirms they copied the new key and CI job now succeeds — thanks! response code 200 and model generated text. :tada:

jordan-cust: quick ask — could the console UI be clearer so admins don't pick the impersonation flow by mistake? we almost tripped over this in onboarding.

nina-support: appreciated feedback — I'll file a UX ticket to add clearer labels and a short tooltip about scopes on each key type.

tyler-eng: adding automated server-side hint: when an impersonation key is used on hosted endpoints we can return a more specific error (e.g., `invalid_api_key: key_missing_api_invoke_scope`) rather than generic invalid_api_key. I'll follow up on a PR.

jordan-cust: perfect. closing this thread for us. thanks everyone!
